subject: Help with checking if SEM model is correct

messages.author: f34de3a2c45f540c
messages.subject: Help with checking if SEM model is correct
parts:
Hi there -

I am running an analysis which considers the role of conspiracy theories  and its relationship between stress and anxiety - and controlling for Social status, age, education and political orientation. 

I am tying to get the model correct before I collect data - so I can pre-register the code

However - I am having trouble with coding it correctly (I think) and would be interested if anyone has any tips for this.

require(lavaan)
require(semPlot)

#model syntax
SEM_mod <- '
#Measurement model
Conspiracy =~ BCT1 + BCT2 + BCT3 + BCT4 + BCT5 + BCT6 + BCT7 + BCT8 + BCT9 + BCT10 + BCT11 + BCT12 + BCT13 + BCT14 + BCT15
Stress =~ PSS1 + PSS2 + PSS3 + PSS4 + PSS5 + PSS6 + PSS7 + PSS8 + PSS9 + PSS10
Anxiety =~ GAD1 + GAD2 + GAD3 + GAD4 + GAD5 + GAD6 + GAD7
#Regressions
Conspiracy ~ Stress + Anxiety + SSocial + Age + Ed + Political
Anxiety + Stress ~~ SSocial + Age + Ed + Political
SSocial ~~ Age + Ed + Political
Age ~~ Ed + Political
Political ~~ Ed
'
#Estimate model
fit = sem(SEM_mod)
ordered(TRUE)

#generate model
semPaths(fit,
nCharNodes = 0, #disable abbreviates if set to 0
sizeMan = 3, # size of manifest variables
sizeLat = 8, # size of latent variables
rotation = 2, #rotates the plot
layout = 'tree2', # tree layout options
curve = 1.5, #curve of correlation lines
)

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: Help with checking if SEM model is correct
parts:
Nick,

Registering the code before you collect data is great. But if you want to do so, the best way to test your code is to simulate data. Look into simsem. You don't need to do a full-blown simulation, but you need a plausible dataset (preferably with some missingness).

Also, there's no need for the ~~ lines. It appears your structural model is essentially a multiple regression, and the exogenous variables will freely covary using the sem() call. If you do 'bring them into the model" this way, you may need to add Anxiety ~~ Stress.

Pat
